quickAnswer: Four in ten Medfield housing units, 1,831 of 4,583, were built from 1960 to 1979, and utility gas heats 56.6% of occupied homes, 14th of 50. A heating or cooling swap here usually means fitting new equipment to a house from the 1960 to 1979 band.
body: ## The 1960 to 1979 band built this town

According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS 2022), the biggest age band in Medfield is 1960 to 1979, with 1,831 of 4,583 housing units, or 40.0%. The median home dates to 1972, 23rd from the oldest among the 50 towns we serve and a few years newer than the 1975 median of the middle town.

Homes built before 1980 total 2,882 (62.9%), which ranks 15th. Yet only 483 units, 10.5%, date from 1939 or earlier, and that share ranks 43rd. In other words, Medfield has few very old houses and many mid-century ones. Another 971 units come from 1980 to 1999 (21.2%), 730 from 2000 or later (15.9%) and 568 from 1940 to 1959 (12.4%).

A house from the 1960 to 1979 band was often designed around a particular heating setup, and the original layout of pipes or ducts shapes what can replace it. Because load depends on insulation, windows and floor plan rather than on age alone, we assess the home's heating load before quoting a system.
## Gas leads, oil follows, and propane has a real foothold

Of 4,463 occupied homes, 2,525 use utility gas (56.6%, 14th of 50, against 41.9% for the middle town) and 1,251 use fuel oil or kerosene (28.0%, 31st). Electricity heats 437 homes (9.8%). Bottled or tank gas heats 239 homes, 5.4% and 19th of 50, above the 4.5% of the middle town.

That bottled gas figure is the unusual one. A home on LP depends on a delivered fuel just as an oil home does, so for those 239 households the question of a heat pump or a gas conversion deserves a look at every replacement.
## Detached houses and high values

Detached single-family houses are 3,843 of the town's units (83.9%), 14th among the 50 towns. Owners hold 3,861 households (86.5%) and renters 602 (13.5%). The median value of an owner-occupied home is $836,400, 11th of 50 and far above the $579,150 of the middle town. With values like that, the choice of equipment is a decision for the long run, and a free written estimate before work starts makes comparison easy.
## From New Dedham to the 43rd town

The land was Neponset territory before English settlement, and the General Court granted Dedham's request for the land west of the Charles River on October 23, 1649. Medfield, then called New Dedham, was first settled that year, and the first 13 house lots were laid out on June 19, 1650. Town Meeting voted to release the village on January 11, 1651, and Medfield became the 43rd town in Massachusetts.

In 1675, during King Philip's War, half the town was destroyed: 32 houses, two mills and many barns. The Peak House burned in the war and was rebuilt shortly afterward near downtown. The town today covers 14.6 square miles, only 0.62% of it water, and sits about 17 miles southwest of Boston.
## Rebates and the meter

Heat pump programs differ by electric utility, and the one for your address has to be confirmed. The [heat pump page](/cities/medfield/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) applies the numbers to Medfield's fuel mix.

faq.q: My Medfield house dates from the 1960 to 1979 band. What should I expect when replacing the heating system?
faq.a: Expect the old layout to guide the choice. That 1960 to 1979 band holds 1,831 Medfield units, and pipes, ducts and radiators were laid out for earlier equipment. The new unit must fit the house, which is why the load is assessed first and a written estimate shows the size, type and work involved.

faq.q: I heat with propane in Medfield. Is that unusual?
faq.a: It is more common here than in the middle town: bottled or tank gas heats 5.4% of Medfield homes, 239 households, against 4.5% for the middle town. Propane is a delivered fuel, so a heat pump or a gas hookup, if a main is available, is a reasonable comparison at the next replacement.

faq.q: Does Medfield's high median home value change the equipment I should choose?
faq.a: It tends to raise the stakes of the decision more than it changes the options. At $836,400, the 11th-highest median value of 50 towns, a house is a major asset, and equipment is chosen to last. Compare written estimates for a like-for-like swap and for a heat pump before committing.

faq.q: Which heat pump rebate would apply to my Medfield home?
faq.a: That depends on the electric utility serving the address, so confirm it before anything else. The program, the weatherization condition and the installer requirement all follow from that. Terms can change, so check masssave.com or ask your utility, and have the written estimate list the size and number of zones.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Medfield burns utility gas in 2,525 homes, oil or kerosene in 1,251 and bottled gas in 239. Each group has its own replacement route, and gas equipment brings a permit and an inspection.
body: ## Fuel by fuel

The ACS 2022 counts 2,525 Medfield homes on utility gas, 1,251 on oil or kerosene, 437 on electricity and 239 on bottled or tank gas. The plan for a failed boiler depends mostly on which of those four describes the house.

On gas, the work is usually a matching swap with attention to venting and the gas line. On oil, the choice stretches to include a conversion where a main exists, or a heat pump for some or all of the load. On bottled gas, there is a tank arrangement and a delivered fuel, and some owners look at the same alternatives as oil households do. On electricity, the question is whether a heat pump would do the same job with less power.
### Gas permits

In Massachusetts only licensed plumbers and gas fitters can pull the permit for gas work. A new gas furnace or boiler normally needs that permit and a final inspection. The town's building department is the place to ask about local procedure.
### Rental units

Medfield has 602 renter households (13.5%, 32nd of 50). Rental units must be kept at 68 F during the day and 64 F overnight in the heating season under 105 CMR 410.201, with the landlord paying for heat unless the lease differs. This is not legal advice.
### The 1960 to 1979 houses

Of the 1,831 units in this band, many still have the distribution system they started with, whether that is baseboard, radiators or ducts. Replacing the boiler or furnace may be simple, while changing the distribution is a bigger project, and each step has its own estimate.
### Late-night failures
A call about a cold house at midnight is routine for us: we answer emergency calls 24 hours a day at (508) 786-8755. The written estimate comes before work starts.

faq.q: Can I convert from oil to gas in Medfield?
faq.a: Possibly, if a gas main reaches the street and the utility agrees to connect. Medfield has 2,525 gas homes, so many of your neighbors may already be on a main, but that does not guarantee yours. Ask the gas company, then compare the connection cost and a new gas unit with a heat pump and a new oil boiler.

faq.q: What happens if my landlord will not fix the heat in Medfield?
faq.a: Put the request in writing and keep a copy. The state sanitary code sets minimum temperatures for the heating season, and the lease determines who pays for heat. Local boards of health handle complaints. This is general information, not legal advice, so consider asking a tenant advocate for specific help.

faq.q: Is an aging boiler worth repairing?
faq.a: It depends on the part and the cost. A small repair on a reliable unit can make sense, but repeated failures, leaks or a cracked heat exchanger usually mean replacement. Ask for the repair figure and the replacement figure in writing so you are comparing real numbers, not impressions.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Medfield has 3,843 detached houses, 170 townhouses and 570 units in multi-unit buildings, including 393 in buildings of five or more. Cooling choices range from ducted central air to a single ductless head.
body: ## Cooling by building type

The housing stock splits into 3,843 detached houses, 170 attached townhouses, 115 units in two-unit buildings, 62 in buildings of three or four, and 393 in buildings of five or more. At 83.9% detached, Medfield ranks 14th for that share, while its multi-unit share of 12.4% ranks 35th.
### Detached homes

A detached house has the room outside for a condenser and, in many cases, room inside for ducts. Some houses have attic or basement space that a duct run can use and others do not, so a site visit settles it.
### Small buildings and larger complexes

Duplexes and three- and four-unit buildings often cool one unit at a time. In a building of five or more, placement of outdoor equipment is usually a matter for the owner or association, so ask for the rules before you plan.
### Newer construction

Medfield counts 730 units from 2000 or later, including 330 from 2010 onward. Newer houses are likelier to have a central duct system already. Whether it is adequate for cooling depends on the sizing of the original design.

- Rooms that overheat in the afternoon or evening.
- Where the condenser can go and how long the line set will be.
- Whether a heat pump could cover both seasons.
- Panel capacity for new equipment.
### Sizing for summer

Cooling does two jobs: lowering the temperature and removing moisture. A unit that is far larger than the load shuts off before it has done the second one, and the house feels sticky. A measured load is better than a rule of thumb.
### Diagnosing a weak system

If a house cools poorly, check airflow and the outdoor coil before assuming the compressor is the problem. A technician can tell whether the fix is a cleaning, a small part or a replacement, and the written estimate states which. For electricity-heated homes, 437 in town, see also the [heat pump page](/cities/medfield/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Is my single-level Medfield house a good candidate for ductless?
faq.a: Often, yes, particularly if there are no ducts or the existing ducts are poor. A single-level layout lets a few wall heads reach most rooms. The number of heads and their size follow from the floor plan and the load, so a site visit and a measured calculation come before a number is offered.

faq.q: How do I cool a unit in a five-plus-unit Medfield building?
faq.a: Usually with a ductless or small ducted system sized for the unit, if the building allows exterior equipment. Ask the owner or association about condenser placement, electrical capacity and noise rules first. The written estimate should name where the outdoor piece goes and how refrigerant lines would run.

faq.q: Can I use the same system for heating and cooling?
faq.a: Yes, that is what a heat pump does. In summer it moves heat outside, and in winter it brings heat in. Many owners keep an existing boiler or furnace as backup for the coldest days. The proposal should state how much of the winter load the heat pump is expected to carry.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Medfield has 1,251 oil or kerosene homes, 239 on bottled gas and 437 on electricity, all candidates for a heat pump comparison. The utility serving the address decides which rebate program applies.
body: ## Where a heat pump fits in Medfield

The whole-home heat pump rebate for 2026 is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, and it requires the house to be weatherized first. Eligibility rules are laid out on the [heat pump services page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### The fuel groups

Oil or kerosene heats 1,251 Medfield homes (28.0%) and bottled gas heats 239 (5.4%). Both fuels are delivered, so a heat pump that carries part of the load cuts the number of deliveries. The 437 electric-heat homes (9.8%) can ask whether a heat pump would deliver the same warmth for less electricity. And the 2,525 gas homes can ask whether a heat pump is more useful for cooling and for shoulder-season heating than for a full switch.
### Age bands and weatherization

Houses built from 2000 on, 730 in Medfield, meet the weatherization condition by date alone. Of those, 330 date from 2010 or later, which ranks 31st of 50. The 1,831 units from 1960 to 1979 and the 971 from 1980 to 1999 would need a Home Energy Assessment, which reports the weatherization work it recommends and what it would cost.
### Ducted, ductless or a hybrid

A house from the 1960 to 1979 band may be able to share existing ducts, or it may suit wall heads. A hybrid, in which the old boiler or furnace handles the coldest days, is an option for owners who prefer to keep a known system as backup while a heat pump handles most of the year.
### Sizing

The heat pump must be sized for the coldest days, not just the average ones. We assess the home's heating load before quoting, and the proposal should state the capacity at low outdoor temperatures. See the [cooling page](/cities/medfield/air-conditioning-installation-repair) for the summer side.

faq.q: Is a heat pump a good fit for a Medfield home on propane?
faq.a: It is worth pricing. The town has 239 bottled gas homes, and propane is a delivered fuel with its own price swings. A heat pump can carry much of the heating load and all of the cooling. The weatherization condition and the utility program still apply, so check both before you plan the budget.

faq.q: My Medfield house was built in 2005. Does it qualify automatically?
faq.a: It meets the weatherization condition because it was built in 2000 or later, but the other conditions still apply: installation in 2026 by an eligible installer and the right utility program for the address. Confirm the current terms at masssave.com or with your utility before you sign.

faq.q: What size heat pump does a house from the 1960 to 1979 band need?
faq.a: The size follows from the house, not from its year. Insulation, windows, air leakage and floor area all enter the calculation, and so does the lowest outdoor temperature the unit must handle. Ask for the load figure behind the proposed size, and compare capacity at low temperatures, not only the nominal tonnage.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Medfield has 3,861 owner-occupied households, 1,251 oil or kerosene homes and 239 on bottled gas. Oil gets a yearly cleaning, gas a safety check, and heat pumps a look at coils, filters and drains.
body: ## A routine for 3,861 owner households
Owners hold 86.5% of Medfield's households, and a house that is lived in is a house where a small problem is noticed early. A planned visit before each season still beats a call in the middle of one.
### Fuel-specific service

Oil systems, 1,251 in town, want a yearly cleaning with the nozzle and filter changed and the combustion tested. Gas systems, 2,525 homes, want a check of the burner, venting and controls. Bottled gas homes, 239 of them, add a tank and regulator to the list. Heat pumps and electric systems need their coils, filters and drains inspected.
### Equipment in a 1960 to 1979 house

The median Medfield home dates to 1972. A heating system in an older house may have been replaced once or twice, and parts for very old units can be harder to find. Use the visit to ask the technician how many seasons the unit may still give, so a replacement can be planned instead of forced.
### Vacant units
Medfield has 120 vacant housing units, a 2.6% vacancy rate. A house that is empty for a season, say between owners, benefits from a pre-winter check so that no one finds a problem after a cold week.

- **Early fall:** heating service, new filter, bleed radiators if you have them.
- **Spring:** cooling check, clear the outdoor unit of leaves and debris.
- **Anytime:** soot, strange smells or a carbon monoxide alarm means stop and call.
### Between visits and what to note

Write down the date of each service and any change you notice, such as a longer run time or a new sound. A short log makes it easier for a technician to spot a pattern, and it helps when you compare the repair history against a replacement estimate.
### The habits that help

Keep snow and leaves from the outdoor unit, change filters on schedule and look at the thermostat settings and batteries before calling about a no-heat problem. When you call, have the fuel type, system age and make and model ready. For replacement questions, see the [heating page](/cities/medfield/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often should a Medfield oil boiler be cleaned?
faq.a: Once a year, in late summer or early fall. The cleaning covers the burner, nozzle, filter and combustion test. Medfield has 1,251 oil or kerosene homes, so this is a regular chore for more than a quarter of the town, and skipping it risks soot buildup and a failure during the coldest weeks.

faq.q: Do bottled gas systems need service too?
faq.a: Yes. A propane boiler or furnace needs the same burner, venting and controls check as any gas unit, and the tank, regulator and piping deserve a look for leaks or damage. If you ever smell gas, leave the house and call the gas supplier or fire department from outside.

faq.q: What is worth doing before a house sits empty for the winter?
faq.a: Have the heating system tested, set a safe minimum temperature and arrange for someone to check the house in a cold spell. An unattended house can freeze a pipe within hours of a heat failure. The visit costs far less than the damage, so treat the empty months as a reason for service.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Medfield's age bands run from 483 units dated 1939 or earlier to 730 dated 2000 or later, with 1,831 in the middle. The Charles River borders almost one-third of the town, so moisture deserves attention.
body: ## Five age bands, five airflows

Medfield's 4,583 housing units divide as follows in the ACS 2022: 483 from 1939 or earlier, 568 from 1940 to 1959, 1,831 from 1960 to 1979, 971 from 1980 to 1999 and 730 from 2000 or later. Each group moves air its own way.
### The 1960 to 1979 core

Houses from these decades often leak at windows, doors and attic hatches, though less than the oldest ones. Before a renovation touches older materials, a qualified specialist should test them, and sealing air leaks afterward can change how much ventilation the house needs.
### Newer and tighter
The 730 units built since 2000 are likelier to be tight. Tight houses hold in cooking fumes and humidity unless fans and ventilation work as intended. Bath fans and range hoods should vent outdoors.
### A town beside a river

The Charles River borders almost one-third of Medfield, and the town's area of 14.6 square miles includes 0.62% water. Houses near water or low ground can have damp basements, and a damp basement raises humidity throughout the house. Fix the water source first, then dry the air.
### Neighbors on all sides

Medfield is surrounded by Dover, Norfolk, Walpole, Millis and Sherborn, and the Charles River marks the Millis border. For air quality, that matters only to the extent that wet areas and tree cover affect pollen and mold spores.
### Moisture and the seasons

In winter, heating dries the air and a humidifier may help, while in summer the same house may need dehumidifying. A humidity reading taken in both seasons shows which way your house leans, and it keeps you from treating a problem you do not have.
### Choices to discuss

- Filtration matched to the airflow of your system.
- A dehumidifier in the basement, once leaks are addressed.
- Ventilation for tight houses.
- Duct cleaning only when ducts show dirt or damage.
Measurements of humidity, carbon monoxide and particles are snapshots, so treat them as clues. For equipment questions, see the [heating page](/cities/medfield/heating-installation-repair).

faq.q: My Medfield basement smells musty. Is that an air quality problem?
faq.a: It can be, since mold and damp materials affect the air upstairs. Look for the water source first: a leak, a grading problem or condensation. A dehumidifier helps with humidity but does not stop a leak. If you see mold or the smell persists, ask a specialist to assess it.

faq.q: Would a whole-house air cleaner help?
faq.a: It may, depending on the problem. Filtration helps with particles like dust and pollen but does little for moisture or carbon monoxide. Ask what you want to fix, then choose the tool. Matching filters to your system's airflow matters, because a very dense filter can restrict air.

faq.q: Should houses built after 2000 have ventilation checked?
faq.a: It is worth a look. Tight houses can trap humidity and cooking fumes. Medfield has 730 units from 2000 or later, and for them a working bath fan, a range hood that vents outside and a plan for fresh air are good basics. A humidity reading in winter shows how well the house breathes.
